evidence: src/warehouse/tracking/dtos/create-delivery.dto.ts: CreateDeliveryDto has orderId, truckId and targetPickUpPoint, each marked @IsString()
src/warehouse/tracking/dtos/update-delivery.dto.ts: UpdateDeliveryDto has id, plus orderId?, truckId? and targetPickUpPoint?, each marked @IsString()
Both files import only class-validator and are used only by tracking.controller.ts and tracking.service.ts, so they cover a single Delivery payload concern
UpdateDeliveryDto repeats the fields instead of deriving from CreateDeliveryDto, and its optional fields have no @IsOptional(): small redundancy plus a validation bug, but not a split concern
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files share one concern: the request payloads for creating and updating a Delivery in warehouse tracking. Both use the same approach, class-validator decorators on plain classes, and only depend on class-validator. Neither bypasses an abstraction or mixes in an unrelated concern. UpdateDeliveryDto declares the same three fields again (orderId, truckId, targetPickUpPoint) instead of building on CreateDeliveryDto, for example with PartialType. That repetition is small and common for create/update DTO pairs, so it isn't a domain rule duplicated in the sense the rubric means. There is a separate issue outside this rule: the optional fields in UpdateDeliveryDto have @IsString() but no @IsOptional(). The validator will therefore reject them when they are missing, even though the type marks them optional. That is a correctness bug, not a cohesion failure, but deriving the update DTO from the create DTO would fix both the repetition and the bug.
